detail.longDescription: I want to be able to check if somebody presses a number key (0 through 9), but only print the key once, and not receive any other inputs until the key is released. I tried using pygame key events for this, but I could not get it to work for some reason, so instead I am using keyboard and a Boolean. To check for release I am utilizing pygame.event.get() and checking for KEYUP Currently, the code prints the first number pressed, and then stops printing any other characters. Here is the code snippet: import pygame import keyboard pygame.init() gamestate = True pressing = False clock = pygame.Clock() print('') while gamestate: for n in range(0, 9): if keyboard.is_pressed(f'{n}') and pressing == False: print(f'{n}') pressing = True break for event in pygame.event.get(): if event.type == pygame.KEYUP: pressing = False clock.tick(60) If it matters, I'm using pygame ce (pygame community edition) for other reasons and the regular python keyboard module.
